claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

is_adopting.description: Whether the claimant is adopting the child.

child_has_moved_in.description: Whether the child being adopted has come to live with the claimant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions.

Let me start by asking: **Do you have any children that you're responsible for?** If yes, could you please tell me how many children you have and their ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hello! Yes, I'm responsible for one child - his name is Alex and he's 18 years old. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. To assess whether you can claim Child Benefit for Alex, I need to understand his current situation since he's 18 years old.

**Is Alex currently in full-time approved education or training?** For example, is he studying A-levels, Scottish Highers, or doing other approved full-time education or training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's still in education - he's studying for his A-levels at sixth form college.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's helpful, thank you. Since Alex is 18 and in full-time education, I need to know a bit more detail.

**When did Alex turn 18, and is he still enrolled in his A-level course?** Also, do you know when his course is due to finish?

This is important because there are specific rules about Child Benefit for 18-year-olds in education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He turned 18 a few months back, and yes, he's still enrolled in his A-levels. The course should finish at the end of the academic year - so around next summer.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. I need to ask one more specific question to determine eligibility:

**Which specific week did Alex turn 18?** More precisely, what was his date of birth? This is important because Child Benefit for young people aged 16-19 in approved education or training stops on the 31st August (known as the "terminal date") following their 18th birthday, or when they leave education, whichever comes first.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, I see. Let me think... he was born in March, so he turned 18 in March of this year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Thank you for that information. Let me first review the official rules to ensure I give you accurate guidance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for waiting. I have a couple more questions to complete my assessment:

1. **Do you live in the UK?**
2. **Does Alex live with you?**

These are important factors for Child Benefit eligibility.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. But no, Alex doesn't live with me at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since Alex doesn't live with you, I need to understand more about your situation:

**Are you contributing financially towards Alex's upkeep?** For example, are you paying for things like food, clothes, pocket money, or contributing towards his accommodation? If yes, approximately how much do you contribute per week or month?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I do help out financially. I contribute towards his upkeep - things like clothes, food, that sort of thing. I give about £30 a week.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. That's helpful to know. I have a couple more questions:

1. **Who does Alex currently live with?** (For example, does he live with another parent, a relative, in student accommodation, etc.)

2. **Is anyone else currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He lives with his other parent - my ex-partner. But no, they're not claiming Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me just clarify one final detail to make sure I have a complete picture:

**When exactly does Alex's A-level course finish?** You mentioned around next summer - will it end before or after 31st August of next year?

This is important because there's a specific "terminal date" rule for Child Benefit when a young person turns 18 while in education.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: It'll finish before the end of August - the course ends when the academic year finishes, so that'll be around late June or early July next year.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for providing all that information. Let me now assess Alex's eligibility for Child Benefit based on what you've told me.

Based on the official guidance I've reviewed, here's my assessment:

**Key facts:**
- Alex turned 18 in March of this year
- He is currently studying A-levels (approved education)
- His course will finish in June/July next year
- He lives with his other parent (your ex-partner)
- You contribute £30 per week towards his upkeep
- No one is currently claiming Child Benefit for Alex
- You live in the UK

**The critical issue:** According to the rules, Child Benefit for young people aged 16-19 in approved education stops on **31st August following their 18th birthday**. Since Alex turned 18 in March of this year, Child Benefit eligibility would end on 31st August of this year - even though his A-level course continues beyond that date.

This means that as of now (after August 31st of this year), Alex has passed the terminal date for Child Benefit eligibility, regardless of whether he's still in education.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
**I'm sorry, but you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex.**

The reason is that although Alex is still in approved full-time education (his A-levels), he turned 18 in March of this year. Under UK Child Benefit rules, eligibility for young people aged 16-19 in approved education ends on **31st August following their 18th birthday**, regardless of whether they continue in education beyond that date.

Since Alex turned 18 in March, his Child Benefit eligibility ended on 31st August of this year, even though his A-level course continues until next summer.

While your £30 weekly contributions towards his upkeep do meet the requirement for claiming when a child lives elsewhere, this doesn't extend the eligibility beyond the 31st August terminal date for 18-year-olds in education.

If you have any questions about this decision or need further clarification, I'd be happy to help.
